# blkit

> A Go SDK for expressing and executing business rules and processes.

## Documentation
- [Home](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/): A Go SDK for expressing and executing business rules and processes in code.
- [Getting started](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/getting-started/): Orientation for new users — what blkit is, when to reach for it, and how to run your first example.
- [Installation](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/installation/): How to add blkit to your Go project and pin it to a known version.
- [Tutorials](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/tutorials/): Guided, narrative walkthroughs that build a working artefact step by step.
- [Templates](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/templates/): Ready-to-copy project scaffolds and boilerplate patterns for common use cases.

## Examples
- [Loan Eligibility](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/loan-eligibility/): A retail bank decides whether a personal loan application is approved, conditionally approved, or declined — and on what terms — from the applicant's credit profile.
- [Shipping Rate Calculator](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/shipping-rate/): An e-commerce platform calculates the total shipping charge for a parcel from billable weight, destination zone, speed tier, and a fuel surcharge — composed entirely from blkit expressions.
- [Order Fulfillment Process](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/order-fulfillment/): An e-commerce platform handles an order from placement through stock reservation, payment, picking, dispatch, and delivery — with explicit branches for out-of-stock and payment-failure cases.
- [Employee Expense Approval](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/expense-approval/): An employee submits a business expense claim; the approval route — automatic, manager, or finance director — is determined by amount, category, and the employee's seniority, then the matching review runs.
- [SaaS Subscription Pricing Engine](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/product-pricing/): A SaaS company calculates the final per-seat price and total monthly charge for a subscription from plan, billing cycle, seat count, loyalty tier, and an optional promo code — four compounding discount factors.
- [Invoice Processing Workflow](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/invoice-processing/): An accounts payable team runs three concurrent validation checks on a supplier invoice, assigns GL codes, routes for amount-based approval, and schedules payment.
- [Employee Onboarding](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/employee-onboarding/): When a new employee is hired, IT, HR, and Facilities run their setup tasks in parallel; the process completes only when all three signal readiness, and escalates if any misses the five-business-day deadline.
- [Insurance Claim Assessment](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/insurance-claim/): A motor insurer assesses a claim's eligibility, scores the damage severity, and calculates a settlement offer — referring high-value settlements to a senior assessor.
- [Customer Discount Eligibility](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/customer-discount/): A pricing engine evaluates an order against many discount rules, collects every rule that matches, and applies the single highest percentage — discounts do not stack.
- [Product Return and Refund](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/product-return/): A customer requests a return; the process validates eligibility within the return window, grades the item's condition on receipt, and issues a refund, replacement, or store credit accordingly.
- [Australian Personal Income Tax Calculator](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/examples/aus-personal-income-tax/): An accounting service calculates an individual's annual income tax liability for FY 2024–25 — building taxable income from many sources, applying progressive brackets, levies, offsets, and HELP/HECS, then reconciling against amounts already paid.

## Expressions
- [Overview](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/overview/): What blkit's expression language is, where it comes from, and the complete set of values it works with — its literal syntax at a glance, and how to test a value's type.
- [Numbers](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/numbers/): Exact decimal arithmetic and the numeric functions — literals, operators, rounding, absolute value, powers, predicates, and more.
- [Strings](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/strings/): Working with text — concatenation, substring, search and replace, case conversion, and formatting functions.
- [Booleans & Logic](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/booleans-and-logic/): Boolean values and blkit's three-valued (true / false / null) logic, including and, or, not, and comparison results.
- [Dates & Times](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/dates-and-times/): Dates, times, date-times, durations, and calendars — construction, arithmetic, component access, and comparisons in the expression language.
- [Lists](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/lists/): Ordered collections and the comprehensions (for, some, every) and functions that operate over them.
- [Dictionaries](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/dictionaries/): Key-value structures — construction, member access, and the dictionary functions.
- [Ranges](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/ranges/): Intervals like `[1..10]` — membership tests, open and closed bounds, the point/interval relations, and how ranges drive unary tests.
- [Tables](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/tables/): Tabular data and the expression-language syntax that filters, projects, groups, and aggregates it.
- [Unary Tests](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/unary-tests/): A compact syntax for writing a condition about a single value — `> 5`, `[18..65]`, `"gold"` — where the value being tested is supplied implicitly.
- [User-Defined Functions](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/user-defined-functions/): Named, reusable functions you define once and call by name from inside any expression — with typed parameters and a typed result.
- [Values from Go](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/expressions/values-from-go/): Constructing blkit values in host Go code, declaring typed environments, and reading results back — the bridge between the expression language and the Go program that runs it.

## Decisions
- [Decision Expressions](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/decisions/decision-expressions/): Compute several named outputs from typed inputs, wiring outputs that depend on one another into a single evaluated unit.
- [Decision Tables](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/decisions/decision-tables/): Express decision logic as a table of rules — rows of input conditions mapped to output values — the spreadsheet-style core of DMN.
- [Decision Native Functions](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/decisions/decision-native-fn/): Back a decision with a hand-written Go function when its logic is beyond — or better expressed outside — the expression language.
- [Sub-Decisions](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/decisions/sub-decisions/): Compose decisions by invoking one decision as a step inside another, so shared logic is defined once and reused.
- [Reference Data](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/decisions/reference-data/): Feed decisions the lookup tables and constants they read from — rates, tiers, thresholds — without hard-coding them into rules.
- [Decision Tasks](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/decisions/decision-tasks/): The unit that runs a decision inside a process — how a decision is invoked, given inputs, and its result captured as the task completes.

## Processes
- [Tasks](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/processes/tasks/): The work items a process is built from — service, decision, and user tasks — and how each one executes and hands control on.
- [Gateways](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/processes/gateways/): Branch and merge the flow of a process — exclusive, parallel, and inclusive routing — using blkit expressions on the outgoing flows.
- [Processes](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/processes/processes/): Assemble tasks and gateways into an executable process graph that runs from a start event through to an end event.

## Architecture
- [Expressions](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/architecture/expressions/): blkit's expression language: a FEEL-flavoured language for business logic, built by extending the Expr engine. Where it comes from, and how it compiles and runs.
- [Worker Pools](https://friendly-business-machines.github.io/blkit/architecture/worker-pools/): How blkit runs processes to completion — pools of workers that pull ready tasks, persist state, and handle retries.
